subtopics.title: The Cost Table and the Three Cost Concepts

questions.question: Total cost at zero output is R24. What does this R24 represent?
options: Marginal cost of the first unit
Fixed cost — owed whether or not anything is produced

questions.question: Total cost is R70 at 3 units and R88 at 4 units. The marginal cost of the fourth unit is:
Average cost at 4 units (total cost R88) is:
Why does average cost FALL over the first few units of output?
options: Because the fixed cost is shared across more and more units
Because variable costs vanish at low output

subtopics.title: Building the Revenue Side at a Market Price of R40

questions.question: At a market price of R40, total revenue at 5 units is:
For a price-taking firm, average revenue always equals:
Why is marginal revenue constant at R40 for this firm?
options: Because each extra unit sells at the unchanged market price of R40
Because output is capped at six units
Because the firm spends heavily on marketing

questions.question: Using total revenue minus total cost, profit at 5 units is:
The economist's rule for the profit-maximising output is to produce:
options: Where average cost reaches its minimum
Until total revenue equals total cost
Until marginal revenue equals marginal cost, stopping before MC exceeds MR
As much as the firm's capacity allows

questions.question: The sixth unit has marginal cost R46 against marginal revenue R40. Producing it would:
The firm still earns R74 profit at six units. Why is six NOT the right output?
options: Because fixed costs jump at six units
Because the firm cannot sell six units
Because profit at five units (R80) is higher — the sixth unit itself destroys profit

subtopics.title: Verifying, Graphing and the Habits That Earn Marks

questions.question: How do you verify the profit-maximising output 'from both directions'?
options: Check the last produced unit adds profit (MC below MR) and the next unit would subtract profit (MC above MR)
Compare fixed cost at zero and six units

questions.question: On the graph, the profit-maximising output is found where:
options: The marginal cost curve cuts up through the flat marginal revenue line
Average cost is at its highest

questions.question: Which pair of verbs matches the two derived measures?
options: Average: divide; Marginal: subtract neighbouring totals

subtopics.title: Costs That Sleep and Costs That Work

questions.question: At the boerewors-roll stand, which of these is a cost that 'sleeps' — owed even on a day with no sales?
options: The friend paid to help when the queue grows
The stall fee, gazebo hire and gas bottle

questions.question: 'What did the LAST one cost me?' is answered by:
options: Subtracting the previous row's total cost from this row's total
Adding fixed and variable cost together

questions.question: Total cost is R88 at 4 units and R120 at 5 units. What did the fifth unit cost on its own?
Why does the average cost per unit drop as the first few units are made?
options: Because the sleeping R24 is carved into more slices, so each unit carries a thinner sliver
Because the selling price rises with output
Because the helper works for free at first

subtopics.title: Forty Rand a Roll, Every Single Roll

questions.question: The stand cannot charge R55 and has no need to charge R30 — the market pays R40. This makes it:
Total revenue at 5 rolls, at R40 a roll, is:
Why is average revenue R40 at every output level?
options: Because costs are also flat at R40
Because the stand always sells exactly five rolls
Because R40 is the average of all the stalls' prices
Because income per roll can only be the price each roll sold for

questions.question: Pictured on a graph with rolls along the bottom and rands up the side, marginal revenue for this stand is:
options: A flat line lying level at the R40 mark

subtopics.title: Is the Next One Worth Making?

questions.question: Roll five brings in R40 and costs R32. The stand should:
options: Make it — it still adds R8
Refuse it — the cost is too close to the price

questions.question: Roll six brings in R40 and costs R46. Making it would:
options: Take R6 straight out of the stand's pocket

questions.question: At six rolls the stand still banks R74 of profit. Why is six still the wrong answer?
options: Because five rolls earn R80 — the right question is whether the NEXT one pays, not whether the day is profitable
Because six rolls cannot be sold
Because the stall fee rises at six rolls

questions.question: Described in words, the marginal cost line in this table:
options: Rises in equal steps of R40
Slides from R20 down to R12 by the third roll, then bends sharply up through R18, R32 and R46 — a lopsided hook
